breakpoints.note: First project parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled persisted bytes and materializes the protocol dispatch key for the vulnerable path.

Root cause. When callers build a parse target with `size == 0`, vulnerable `coap_pdu_init()` allocates only `max_hdr_size` bytes and places `pdu->token` exactly at the end of that allocation. The fix changes this allocation to reserve at least two payload bytes so the later extended-token probes in `coap_pdu_parse_header()` cannot read past the buffer.

Crash sink. The extended-token branch dereferences the first token byte even though the accepted WSS packet had no bytes after its two-byte header, so `pdu->token[0]` is one byte past the heap buffer allocated by `coap_pdu_init(..., 0)`.
